title: OBJ export via stream+explicit-options raises a different crash (NotImplementedError from exporter-registration order) than the same save via a file path (TypeError)
repro: python work/obj_stream_tb.py   # scene.save(io.StringIO(), ObjSaveOptions())
Traceback: Scene.py:180 io_service.create_exporter(detected_format) -> IOService.py:52 exporter.supports_format(format_type) -> Exporter.py:14 NotImplementedError: supports_format is not implemented
Contrast: python work/obj_retry_tb.py   # scene.save(path, ObjSaveOptions()) -> TypeError: a bytes-like object is required, not 'str' (same ObjSaveOptions class, different call shape)
expected: Calling Scene.save() with the same, correctly-imported ObjSaveOptions should fail the same way (or succeed) regardless of whether the destination is a file path or an in-memory stream.
actual: The crash signature differs depending on call shape, because IOService.create_exporter() walks a process-global, import-order-dependent _exporters list and calls each exporter's supports_format() in turn; FbxExporter's supports_format() is unconditionally unimplemented and is reached before ObjExporter's in the stream+options case but not in the path case in this test run. This makes OBJ export failures non-deterministic/confusing depending on unrelated earlier imports in a user's program.
suggested_fix: Report to upstream: IOService._exporters is a mutable class-level list populated by import side effects; registration order (and therefore which exporter 'wins' the lookup) is not deterministic across call shapes. Not fully root-caused within the time budget (see report.md); flagging as a secondary symptom of ISS-001.

title: Mesh.createPolygon's (indices, offset, length) branch is dead code: a 3-argument call is always intercepted by the earlier 3-raw-numbers branch, so the offset/length call form can never execute
repro: Static read of lib/src/aspose/threed/entities/Mesh.ts, createPolygon(): branch order is (1) single array arg of length 3 or 4 -> recurse as separate numbers, (2) `args.length === 3` -> treat as 3 raw vertex indices v1,v2,v3, (3) `args.length === 4` -> treat as 4 raw vertex indices, (4) `args.length === 3 && typeof args[2] === 'number'` -> treat as (indices[], offset, length). Branch (4) requires args.length===3, which branch (2) already matched and returned from, so (4) is unreachable for any real call.
expected: Every documented/intended call form of createPolygon should be reachable.
actual: Calling createPolygon(indicesArray, offsetNumber, lengthNumber) (3 arguments, 3rd one being a number) is silently interpreted as 3 raw vertex indices (v1=indicesArray, v2=offsetNumber, v3=lengthNumber) instead of the offset/length slice form, because branch (2) fires first. This is purely an upstream TypeScript-port defect (the Python original this was ported from the (list, offset, length) form may have worked because Python branches differently); version is @aspose/3d 24.12.0 at commit 66cb26df3b031f0bf6976d4e88dc89721983afa4.
evidence: (static source read only -- see portfolio/3d-typescript/lib/src/aspose/threed/entities/Mesh.ts in round-1's clone; no MCP evidence file, since the MCP does not surface this)
suggested_fix: For the MCP: flag createPolygon similarly to other partially-broken methods ('the (indices, offset, length) call form is unreachable in this build'). For upstream: reorder the branches so the 3-number-typeof-check happens before the generic 3-args branch, or drop the dead branch.

title: Numeric cell values silently become Go strings after Save+Load round-trip (undisclosed)
repro: go get github.com/aspose-cells-foss/Aspose.Cells-FOSS-for-Go/v26@v26.7.1
In Go: wb := cells_foss.NewWorkbook(); ws := wb.Worksheets[0]; ws.Cells().Set("B2", 1200.0); wb.Save("out.xlsx")
wb2, _ := cells_foss.Load("out.xlsx"); c, _ := wb2.Worksheets[0].Cells().Get("B2"); fmt.Printf("%v (%T)", c.Value, c.Value)
Full repro committed at PILOTDIR/work/t6/main.go (run via: go build -o app.exe . && ./app.exe)
Independently verified saved XML is CORRECT (xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml has <c r="B2"><v>1200</v></c> with no t="s" attribute, i.e. valid OOXML numeric cell) -- the bug is in the loader, not the saver.
python -I -c "import zipfile; print(zipfile.ZipFile('scenario_out.xlsx').read('xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml').decode())"  (see PILOTDIR/evidence and work/t6/scenario_out.xlsx)
expected: Reloading a workbook that was saved with Cells().Set(ref, 1200.0) (float64) should return cell.Value as a numeric type (float64), matching both the OOXML spec (an untyped <c> is numeric) and the library's own Cells.Set doc comment.
actual: cell.Value comes back as the Go string "1200" (type string), not float64(1200). Confirmed in library source aspose/cells_foss/xmlloader.go, function resolveCellValue: the comment literally reads '// Numeric or untyped — return as string; callers may parse with strconv.' Every numeric cell in every reloaded workbook is affected, including CalculateFormula's own cellToFloat() needing a fallback string-to-float parse to compensate.
suggested_fix: Upstream: resolveCellValue should parse <v> to float64 (or int64) when c.T is empty or "n". A coding agent that does cell.Value.(float64) after any Load() will panic; one that does naive string concatenation on reloaded numbers will silently produce wrong output.

python3 -c "print(open('scenario_out.csv','rb').read(4))"  -> b'PK\x03\x04' (ZIP/OOXML signature)

This is exactly the 'wrong information that makes a newcomer's code fail silently' class of defect: the MCP's own install/limitations text invites exactly this mistake by documenting 'Added automatic PDF format selection in Workbook.Save(string fileName) when the output path ends with .pdf' (from list_recent_changes V26.9.0) without ever saying what happens for every OTHER extension.
suggested_fix: Upstream: Workbook.Save(string) should throw an explicit exception (e.g. UnsupportedFeatureException, which already exists in the public API) when the file extension does not correspond to a supported SaveFormat, instead of silently defaulting to XLSX bytes. # cellXfs: xf s=1 (A1, '#,##0.00') -> numFmtId="0" (General, WRONG); xf s=2 (A2, '$#,##0.00') -> numFmtId="164" (correct custom numFmt); xf s=3 (A3, '0%') -> numFmtId="0" (General, WRONG)

actual: workbook.ts's generateStyles() has: `if (style.numberFormat && !builtinFmts.includes(style.numberFormat)) { ...register custom numFmtId... }` with builtinFmts = ["General","0","0.00","#,##0","#,##0.00","0%","0.00%","0.00E+00"]. title: Cell.putValue(ref, Date) writes an Excel serial date that is off by one day
repro: cd portfolio2/cells-typescript/work && tsx t6_scenarios.ts   # s1.putValue('C2', new Date(2024,0,15))
python -I -c "import zipfile; print(zipfile.ZipFile('out_scenarioA.xlsx').read('xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml').decode())"   # <c r="C2"><v>45305</v></c>
python -I -c "import datetime; epoch=datetime.date(1899,12,30); print((datetime.date(2024,1,15)-epoch).days)"   # 45306, the correct Excel serial for 2024-01-15
expected: Excel serial 45306 for 2024-01-15 (1899-12-30 epoch, 1900 date system).
actual: Excel serial 45305 was written -- one day short. cell.ts's dateToExcelSerial() computes `Math.floor((date.getTime() - excelEpoch.getTime()) / 86400000)` using two local-time Date objects 124 years apart; this naive subtraction is vulnerable to historical local-time/DST-table artifacts and produced a wrong serial in this environment.
suggested_fix: Compute the day difference using UTC-normalized dates (e.g. Date.UTC(y,m,d) for both the value and the epoch) instead of local-time millisecond subtraction, to make the serial independent of the runtime's timezone/DST history.

title: Embedded message attachment is serialized to EML as a CFB/.msg binary blob mislabeled 'message/rfc822' (base64) instead of a real RFC822 message
repro: Build the indexed commit c844a467cf7f2503819b655f4d6ceaef91056c40 with CMake+Ninja+MSVC (install section's FetchContent snippet).

auto msg = mapi_message::create(subject, body, true); msg.add_embedded_message_attachment(mapi_message::create("Embedded subject","Embedded body", true), "embedded.msg", "message/rfc822"); msg.save_to_eml("scen.eml");

python -I -c "import email,base64; from email import policy; m=email.message_from_bytes(open('scen.eml','rb').read(), policy=policy.default); outer=m.get_payload()[3]; print(outer['Content-Type'], outer['Content-Transfer-Encoding']); inner=outer.get_payload()[0]; b64=inner.get_payload(); d=base64.b64decode(b64.replace(chr(10),'')); print(d[:8].hex())"
expected: The message/rfc822 attachment part should contain a real, textual RFC822 message (parseable headers: Subject: Embedded subject, From, body text 'Embedded body'), per RFC 2046/2045 (message/* must use 7bit/8bit/binary transfer-encoding, never base64/quoted-printable).
actual: The part is declared 'Content-Type: message/rfc822; name="embedded.msg"' with 'Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64'. Decoding that base64 payload yields 3072 raw bytes starting with hex d0cf11e0a1b11ae1 - the CFB/OLE2 (.msg) file magic number. The embedded message's own Subject header reads back as None when parsed by a standards-compliant client (Python's email module) because the payload is not text - it is a binary MSG file disguised as an email body. No real mail client or RFC822 parser can read the embedded message's subject/body from this attachment.
suggested_fix: The EML/MIME writer (src/msg/mime/eml_message_mapper.cpp in the indexed repo) should recursively render an embedded mapi_message as its own RFC822 text (headers + body/multipart), not as a serialized CFB/.msg blob; until fixed, the MCP's agent_guidance or limitations section should warn that add_embedded_message_attachment + save_to_eml produces a non-standard, unreadable message/rfc822 part.

title: TiffFormatHandler misreads BitsPerSample for any multi-sample (e.g. RGB) TIFF, returning garbage BitDepth instead of 8
repro: Generate single.tif (33x22 RGB) and multi.tif (3-page 20x20 RGB) with Pillow (work/gen_images.py)
Run work/harness against work/imgs and read work/probe_results.json for single.tif / multi.tif
expected: BitDepth = 8 (standard 8-bit-per-channel RGB TIFF, confirmed via Pillow ground truth mode='RGB')
actual: single.tif -> BitDepth=134; multi.tif -> BitDepth=134. Root cause (src/Aspose.Imaging.Foss/Formats/TiffFormatHandler.cs, ReadIfdValue): tag 258 (BitsPerSample) for an RGB image is a SHORT array with Count=3 (one value per channel), so per the TIFF spec its 6 bytes of data don't fit in the IFD entry's 4-byte value field and that field actually holds an OFFSET to the real data elsewhere in the file. ReadIfdValue never checks the entry's Count field; for type==SHORT it always reads the 4-byte 'value' field as if it held an inline UInt16, so for any count>1 field it decodes the low 16 bits of a file offset as the 'bit depth'.
suggested_fix: ReadIfdValue (or its caller) must check the IFD entry's Count field; when type-size*count > 4, follow the 4-byte value as a file offset and read the real data from there instead of treating it as inline. At minimum, a single-count BitsPerSample (grayscale) will still work; any count>1 case (RGB, RGBA, etc.) needs offset-following.

repro: pip install aspose-note-foss==26.9.0

# fetch a real sample: gh api repos/aspose-note-foss/Aspose.Note-FOSS-for-Python/contents/testfiles/SimpleTable.one?ref=0014dbeef9511af360b936d95d47947d6b1d8a4f --jq '.content' | base64 -d > SimpleTable.one
python -c "
from aspose.note import Document, DocumentVisitor, RichText
class C(DocumentVisitor):
def VisitRichTextStart(self, rt): self.n+=1
doc=Document('SimpleTable.one'); c=C(); doc.Accept(c)
print('visitor saw', c.n, 'GetChildNodes saw', len(doc.GetChildNodes(RichText)))"
# prints: visitor saw 0  GetChildNodes saw 12
expected: A DocumentVisitor that implements VisitRichTextStart counts every RichText node in the document, or the limitations/API docs clearly warn that table contents are invisible to the visitor pattern.
actual: DocumentVisitor.VisitRichTextStart is called 0 times for a table-only document that has 12 real RichText nodes inside its cells (confirmed independently via GetChildNodes(RichText)). get_symbol(aspose.note.DocumentVisitor) confirms the class declares no VisitTableStart/VisitTableRowStart/VisitTableCellStart/VisitAttachedFileStart hooks at all -- Table, TableRow, TableCell and AttachedFile are simply never dispatched. The MCP's own 'Count Nodes With a DocumentVisitor' example (find_examples query='Document') happens to run against 3ImagesWithDifferentAlignment.one, which has no table, so this gap is never exposed by the example, and get_product_reference(section=limitations) does not mention it either.
suggested_fix: Upstream: add Visit*Start/End hooks for Table/TableRow/TableCell/AttachedFile/NumberList to DocumentVisitor so it reaches every node type CompositeNode exposes via GetChildNodes. MCP-side (independent of the upstream fix): add a bullet to get_product_reference(section=limitations), e.g. "DocumentVisitor does not dispatch into Table/TableRow/TableCell or AttachedFile contents; use GetChildNodes(...) directly to reach text or images inside tables."

expected: The tool description says: "Search ... by type name or fragment, e.g. query='Image'" -- implying any genuine substring/prefix of a real type name should surface that type as a match, not merely as a did-you-mean suggestion.
actual: Queries shorter than ~4 characters, and some 5-character exact prefixes (e.g. 'NoteT' of 'NoteTag'), return an explicit miss with only a `suggestions` (did-you-mean) list; the real match is never returned as a result the caller can act on directly. title: RichText.Text extraction leaves a raw OneNote field-separator character and field-instruction text inside hyperlink runs
repro: gh api repos/aspose-note-foss/Aspose.Note-FOSS-for-Python/contents/testfiles/FormattedRichText.one?ref=0014dbeef9511af360b936d95d47947d6b1d8a4f --jq '.content' | base64 -d > FormattedRichText.one
python -c "from aspose.note import Document, RichText; doc=Document('FormattedRichText.one'); print([r.Text for r in doc.GetChildNodes(RichText)])"
# one entry is: 'This is \ufddfHYPERLINK "www.google.com"hyperlink. This text is not a hyperlink.'
expected: RichText.Text should contain only the human-visible display text ("This is hyperlink. This text is not a hyperlink."), matching what OneNote itself shows.
actual: The extracted text embeds a raw Unicode noncharacter (U+FDDF) followed by the literal internal field instruction `HYPERLINK "www.google.com"`, which is Word/OneNote field-code plumbing that should have been consumed, not echoed into the plain-text value. This is exercised by the MCP's own verified 'Extract All Text' example against this exact file, so any agent following that example verbatim gets garbled output and has no way to know it is a known library quirk.
suggested_fix: Upstream: strip or decode OneNote field-code runs (delimited by U+0013/U+0014/U+0015 equivalents in the .one binary format) when building RichText.Text, keeping only the display-text portion. MCP-side: note this as a known text-extraction limitation for hyperlink-containing documents.

text is: '- Read XPS packages with `XpsDocument.from_file()` / from_bytes(), walking fixed pages and
- Write PDF 1.4 output with `PdfWriter`, including TrueType/Type1 font embedding resolved through
- This library converts and authors documents; it does not read existing PDF files (there is no

- Importing `aspose.page.pdf.writer` or `aspose.page.image.raster_renderer` directly, or calling

repro: python -c "import aspose.page.ps; from aspose.page.ps import PsDocument; d=PsDocument.create(); print(len(d.pages)); d.add_page(); print(len(d.pages))"   # prints 1 then 2
python -c "import aspose.page.ps; from aspose.page.xps import XpsDocument; d=XpsDocument.create(); print(len(d.builder.pages))"  # prints 0
python mcpraw.py page-python get_symbol fqn=aspose.page.ps.PsDocument   # docstring/signature say nothing about an initial page
python mcpraw.py page-python lookup query="does PsDocument.create() already contain a page"
python mcpraw.py page-python search_docs query="create already contains a page"   # only hits the unrelated Scope-and-Limitations chunk via keyword overlap
python mcpraw.py page-python search_docs query="add_page duplicate first page"    # explicit miss
python mcpraw.py page-python find_examples query="create a new PS document and add a page"   # explicit miss (no semantic search)
expected: Either the docstring/raw_text for PsDocument.create() states its post-condition on page count, or a troubleshooting/FAQ entry warns that calling add_page() right after create() yields 2 pages, not 1. The same create() naming should behave consistently across PsDocument and XpsDocument, or the difference should be documented.
actual: PsDocument.create() and PsDocument.create(is_eps=True) both return a document with len(doc.pages)==1 already; XpsDocument.create() returns 0 pages. Nothing in get_symbol's raw_text, the formats/limitations/troubleshooting sections, or any of 7 doc/example queries tried states this. An agent following the natural pattern 'create() then add_page() to get page 1' silently ends up with an unwanted second, blank page -- the kind of silent-corruption trap most costly for a newcomer because save()/to_pdf() succeed without error.
suggested_fix: Add one sentence to PsDocument.create()'s docstring ('returns a document that already contains one page; use get_page(0) / pages[0] instead of add_page() to access it') and surface the PsDocument-vs-XpsDocument create() page-count asymmetry in the limitations/troubleshooting doc.

title: Freshness/install notice is anchored only to GitHub tags and cannot see that PyPI's real latest release (26.9.0) has no corresponding git tag at all, so 'fresh' / '5 commits ahead of 26.7.0' materially understates the real version gap between pip install and the index
repro: pip install aspose-page-foss   # installs 26.9.0
curl https://pypi.org/pypi/aspose-page-foss/json   # releases: only '26.9.0', uploaded 2026-09-18T09:59:44Z -- never a '26.7.0' wheel on PyPI
curl https://api.github.com/repos/aspose-page-foss/Aspose.Page-FOSS-for-Python/tags   # only tags 26.7.0 (dac5d70e, 2026-07-24) and 26.5.0 -- no 26.9.0 tag exists anywhere in git
python mcpraw.py page-python get_product_reference section=install
python mcpraw.py page-python report_index_freshness current_source_commit:=null
expected: The freshness/install notice should be able to say, or at least flag as unknown, that the registry's actual latest version has no known source commit to compare against -- i.e. 'package_ahead_of_index: unknown, no tag found for 26.9.0' -- rather than implying the only drift is '5 commits ahead of 26.7.0'.
actual: get_product_reference(install) and report_index_freshness both say only: 'The indexed commit 43cef367cd0b is 5 commits ahead of the latest release 26.7.0' and report freshness_state='fresh', latest_release_tag='26.7.0'. Neither mentions that PyPI's actual latest (26.9.0, what `pip install aspose-page-foss` actually gives you) was published from a commit that was NEVER tagged in git, so there is no way -- via this MCP or via git -- to know whether the indexed API (commit 43cef367, 1 day after the 26.9.0 upload) matches, adds to, or diverges from the code inside the 26.9.0 wheel a user actually gets. freshness_basis='git_ancestry' cannot detect this because it only walks tags/commits, never queries the registry's actual latest version.
suggested_fix: Cross-check the registry's reported latest version (already fetched for the install notice) against the set of git tags; when the registry's latest version has no matching tag, say so explicitly ('registry version 26.9.0 has no corresponding source tag; freshness relative to it is unknown') instead of silently comparing only to the newest tagged release.

title: XpsGlyphs.font_uri accepts any string, including a path to a font that was never added to the XPS package; the renderer silently falls back to a default font instead of erroring, and this fallback behavior is undocumented
repro: python work/ex_xps/try_xps_text.py  # builds XpsDocument.create() -> add_page() -> elements.append(XpsGlyphs(font_uri='/Resources/Fonts/font1.odttf', ...)) where that URI is never registered in the package's parts dict
# to_pdf() and to_image() both succeed; pypdf confirms the PDF page text is 'Hello XPS' and the PNG has non-white glyph pixels, i.e. text rendered despite the font never existing
expected: get_symbol for XpsGlyphs, or the limitations section, states what happens when font_uri does not resolve to a real font part in the package (error vs. fallback vs. silently-wrong glyph shapes), and/or lists valid font_uri formats.
actual: get_symbol('aspose.page.xps.editing.XpsGlyphs') only shows 'font_uri: str (writable)' with no validation, allowed-value list, or behavior note. Empirically, a nonexistent font_uri does not raise; the library silently substitutes a fallback font and still renders the requested unicode_string. An agent has no way to know, from the MCP, whether the glyphs it just rendered actually used the font it asked for.
suggested_fix: Document the font_uri contract: what a valid URI looks like (presumably an OPC part name registered via XpsPackage.parts), and that resolution failures fall back silently rather than raising -- this is exactly the kind of implicit behavior an agent needs stated, not discovered by experiment.

Independently verify with pypdf (venv with pypdf+cryptography): pypdf.PdfReader(encrypted3.pdf, password='user-password').pages[0].extract_text() raises pypdf.errors.PdfReadError: Invalid Elementary Object starting with b';' ... (the AES-decrypted content stream is garbage, not valid PDF operators)

actual: Aspose's own TextAbsorber silently returns an empty string after the round trip (no error, no exception - a silent correctness failure); pypdf, decrypting independently per spec, gets non-PDF garbage bytes from the same content stream, confirming the encryption/decryption implementation itself is non-conformant at this commit. The MCP's 'Open a Password-Protected Document' example already recorded a runtime crash in its own verification field ('fails at runtime: flate: bad zlib header check') but is still returned to callers with no explicit broken/do-not-use flag - only prose buried in the 'verification' string.
evidence: evidence/encrypt_test_encrypted3... (see work/encrypt_test3/main.cpp, plain3.pdf, encrypted3.pdf copied to evidence/plain3.pdf, evidence/encrypted3.pdf)
suggested_fix: File/confirm an upstream bug against Aspose.PDF-FOSS-for-Cpp at commit 4b83c9fec1e37fd205156770161f6843bac00ceb for AESx256 content-stream encryption/decryption; until fixed, have the example curator attach a structured 'broken': true / 'do_not_use' flag (not just free text in 'verification') to any example whose own ingestion-time verification recorded a runtime failure, and have get_product_reference section=limitations mention the AES-256 round-trip defect explicitly.

title: The natural first guess for adding text to a page - page.Paragraphs().Add(TextFragment) - is guaranteed to fail to compile (C2664), and nothing proactively tells a newcomer that TextFragment is not a BaseParagraph before they try it
repro: python mcpraw.py pdf-cpp list_members fqn=Aspose::Pdf::Text::TextFragment   and   list_members fqn=Aspose::Pdf::Paragraphs   -> list_members never shows base classes (by design, documented in its own tool description: 'Base types are NOT included... call get_symbol')

Compiled verbatim (MSVC 19.44, find_package route) the natural guess: page.Paragraphs().Add(TextFragment_instance); -> error C2664: 'void Aspose::Pdf::Paragraphs::Add(Aspose::Pdf::BaseParagraph &)': cannot convert argument 1 from 'Aspose::Pdf::Text::TextFragment' to 'Aspose::Pdf::BaseParagraph &' (full MSVC transcript saved)
expected: Either list_members/search_symbols surfaces the base-class relationship (or its absence) inline, or find_examples/search_docs proactively documents 'TextFragment is not a BaseParagraph - use TextBuilder(page).AppendText(fragment) to place text' before the compile error happens.
actual: get_symbol does correctly return bases: [] for TextFragment, so the fact IS technically discoverable - but only by (1) already suspecting the inheritance is wrong, (2) calling get_symbol specifically on TextFragment (not list_members, which most agents reach for first per its own description), and (3) interpreting an empty bases array as 'therefore not assignable to Paragraphs::Add'. No example or doc states the correct route (TextBuilder.AppendText) up front; find_examples has 0 examples for 'TextFragment', 'text', or 'paragraph'.
suggested_fix: Add a short developer_guide or troubleshooting entry: 'Adding text to a page: TextFragment does not inherit BaseParagraph; use Aspose::Pdf::Text::TextBuilder(page).AppendText(fragment), not page.Paragraphs().Add(fragment).' and/or have search_symbols/list_members mention 'bases: []' context inline instead of requiring a second get_symbol call.
round1_ref: Paragraphs::Add takes BaseParagraph& while TextFragment is not one (round-1 seed, reproduced with exact MSVC error text; nuance added re: get_symbol's bases field)

python mcpraw.py slides-cpp search_symbols query=hyperlink top_k=5   # -> IHyperlinkContainer, match_quality=exact
python mcpraw.py slides-cpp list_members fqn=Aspose::Slides::Foss::IHyperlinkContainer  # -> only one line: the defaulted virtual destructor; zero real members

get_product_reference section=limitations confirms: no charts, no animations/transitions, and 'no set_hyperlink_click on a portion format or a shape' -- all three concepts the queries above asked about are explicitly documented as NOT supported.
expected: For a concept the library genuinely does not support, search_symbols should either return a clean miss (as it correctly does for 'add_slide' and 'SmartArt' in this same index) or, if it must return a lexical near-hit, should not mark it match_quality='exact' when the hit is purely a substring coincidence (ShapeType::CHART_X/CHART_STAR enum members, or a zero-method marker interface like IHyperlinkContainer).
actual: 'chart' exact-matches ShapeType and SlideLayoutType purely because ShapeType declares CHART_X/CHART_STAR/CHART_PLUS enum values (shape outlines, not charts); 'transition' exact-matches EffectFormat/Shape/BasePortionFormat, none of which have anything to do with slide transitions; 'hyperlink' exact-matches IHyperlinkContainer, a completely empty marker interface. title: 'formats'/'limitations' sections assert 7 SaveFormat values 'produce valid output files', but 5 of those 7 write a corrupt (wrong content-type) package in the PyPI release the 'install' section tells you to use
repro: python mcpraw.py slides-python get_product_reference section=limitations
python mcpraw.py slides-python get_product_reference section=formats
pip install aspose-slides-foss   # 26.8.0, same version get_product_reference section=install prescribes

python -c "
import aspose.slides_foss as slides, zipfile, re
from aspose.slides_foss.export import SaveFormat
for name in ['PPTX','PPTM','PPSX','PPSM','POTX','POTM']:
    with slides.Presentation() as prs:
        prs.save(f'ct_{name}.pptx', getattr(SaveFormat, name))
    ct = zipfile.ZipFile(f'ct_{name}.pptx').read('[Content_Types].xml').decode()
    m = re.search(r'PartName=\"/ppt/presentation\\.xml\"[^>]*ContentType=\"([^\"]+)\"', ct)
    print(name, m.group(1))
"
expected: If a section tells an agent that 'only seven SaveFormat values produce valid output files' (PPTX, PPTM, PPSX, PPSM, POTX, POTM, MD), the agent should be able to pip-install the package the 'install' section names and get genuinely valid files for all seven, or be told clearly in that same response that this is true only for the unreleased/default-branch build.
actual: All six non-MD PowerPoint formats save without raising an exception in the installed 26.8.0, but PPTM/PPSX/PPSM/POTX/POTM all declare the SAME main-part content type as PPTX ('...presentationml.presentation.main+xml') instead of their own type -- the exact defect the repository's own CHANGELOG.md (at the indexed commit) describes as fixed only on the unreleased default branch ('PowerPoint can't open this file because its file extension has changed'). agent_guidance does carry a general 'describes the default branch, not 26.8.0' notice, but the 'formats' and 'limitations' tool responses (which make the concrete 'produce valid output files' claim) carry only a commit-id notice, not that same not-yet-released caveat, so an agent that calls only those two sections -- a very natural thing to do -- is told something materially false about the version it was just told to pip install. Only PPTX and MD are genuinely valid in 26.8.0; the installed library reports success (no exception) while silently writing a file many consumers will refuse to open.
suggested_fix: Propagate the install section's 'installed package may differ from the indexed commit' notice into every get_product_reference section whose text makes a version-sensitive behavioral claim (formats, limitations), not just 'install'; or state explicitly, next to the 'seven SaveFormat values' claim, which of the seven are confirmed valid in the currently-published registry version.

title: MCP's own extraction/coverage note ('11 of 45 source files could not be parsed') understates the real breakage by roughly 3x and gives false confidence the library is mostly usable
repro: python -I mcpraw.py tex-python report_index_freshness --save evidence/freshness.json   # coverage_note: '11 of 45 source files could not be parsed'

The '21 of 21 types' coverage ratio is also circular: total_types is set equal to indexed_types rather than to an independently-counted true total, so '100% coverage' is true by construction and tells the caller nothing about the roughly 80+ real classes (public and private) that exist in the 35 broken files and are invisible to the index.

The MCP should flag this discrepancy in get_product_reference(limitations) once confirmed, since it is exactly the kind of silent-data-loss gotcha that section already documents well for SaveFormat.DOC and OoxmlCompliance.

title: Paragraph/HeaderFooter 'children' (the only way to add Run/Table content) is implemented via a private-attribute pydantic wrap-validator that the source code's own docstring calls 'intentionally not part of the public attribute surface' - undocumented anywhere a user or the MCP can find
repro: Read aspose/words_foss/light_document_model.py:639-658: Paragraph's _children is a PrivateAttr; the class docstring explicitly says 'The collection itself is intentionally not part of the public attribute surface.'

work/try_builder.py ATTEMPT1: `ldm.Paragraph(children=[ldm.Run(text='Hello world')])` - works despite the field not being declared, because the `_absorb_children` model_validator(mode='wrap') intercepts the 'children' kwarg from the input dict pydantic builds internally.
python -I mcpraw.py words-python get_symbol fqn=aspose.words_foss.light_document_model.Paragraph  # properties list does not mention 'children' as a constructible field at all
expected: If this is the intended (if unofficial) way to add Run/BookmarkStart/Shape content to a Paragraph when building documents programmatically, either the MCP's symbol data or its docs should mention it, since it's the single most important mechanic for the builder path identified in WORDS-PY-001.
actual: get_symbol's properties/methods listing for Paragraph has no 'children' entry (correctly, since it is a PrivateAttr) and no narrative anywhere states that passing `children=[...]` as a constructor kwarg is the supported way to populate it. A newcomer reading only the MCP would have no way to discover this mechanic even after finding LdmDocxWriter.
suggested_fix: Once WORDS-PY-001's from-scratch example is added, make sure it explicitly shows the `children=[...]` construction idiom so agents don't have to reverse-engineer the wrap-validator from source.

actual: The snippet is presented as example code with no truncation marker on the base64 literal (only the general 'compiled only, not run-verified' caveat applies). An agent copy-pasting it verbatim gets a decode failure unrelated to the real API.

title: Self-reported API-Coverage ('272 of 272 types; 119 of 119 functions') could not be independently reconciled with a live pkgutil/inspect enumeration of the installed package
repro: work/enumerate_all.py: walks every aspose.words_foss submodule via pkgutil.walk_packages + vars(), counting classes/functions whose __module__ equals the defining module -> 209 classes, 124 functions

work/enumerate_all2.py: same walk but counting unique class/function objects (by id()) restricted to aspose.words_foss ownership, counting re-exports once -> 205 classes, 309 functions (lower-level private helpers included)
python -I mcpraw.py words-python report_index_freshness  # indexed_types: 272, total_types: 272
expected: A stated coverage ratio should be reproducible by an independent enumeration of the same package at the same commit, or the methodology (e.g. counting every exported FQN alias as a separate 'type') should be documented so the ratio is checkable.
actual: Neither counting method (per-owning-module, or per-unique-object) lands on 272 types / 119 functions; both are lower for types (205-209) and inconsistent for functions depending on whether private helpers are included (124 vs 309). This is reported at LOW/MEDIUM confidence since the gap is plausibly explained by the indexer counting each re-exported FQN alias as a distinct 'type' (observed: the same LdmDocxWriter class is indexed under at least 2 FQNs), which my enumeration intentionally de-duplicates - but this could not be confirmed without seeing the indexer's own counting code.
suggested_fix: Document the exact counting methodology behind 'API-Coverage: N of N types' (per-FQN-alias vs per-unique-symbol) so downstream auditors and agents can verify the ratio rather than taking it on faith.
